text:
ops-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: runtime-streamer: cont-batch streaming p99 spike detected (>5s) in us-west-2. SLO monitor triggered. Deploy tag: release/1.14.2. Affected routes: /v1/stream (high volume), ~0.8% of traffic. Paging oncall.

sara_p: seeing it on my end too. p95 ~220ms, p99 ~5.7s. Any recent config changes to batching? :thinking_face:

mike_h: yes we pushed a perf tweak earlier that increased max_batch_size for streamer pool from 16->32 to improve throughput. Rollout finished 25m ago. Grafana: https://grafana.redwood/runtime-streamer/alerts/178945 (short link)

lee_ops: running quick checks — queue lengths spiking on packer-0/1. Running:
```
kubectl exec -n prod streamer-packer-0 -- bash -lc "curl -s localhost:9100/metrics | grep packer_queue_len"
# returns 820, 930
```
Looks like packing delay, big batches waiting, then one long flush causes tail blowup.

nina_re: could be mixed-seqlen amplification — long sequences block packer, others wait and then get flushed in huge batch.

sara_p: agree. Customer impact: we have 3 customers with latency alarms (internal tags). No 5xxs. Recommend immediate mitigation: cap max_batch_size to 8 on streaming pool and lower batching flush timeout to 50ms to favor low-latency.

tim_oncall: +1 to mitigation. If throughput drops significantly we can open short burst capacity but prefer latency fix now. I'll page infra if we need extra nodes. @mike_h can you roll a canary change to 10% of streamer nodes first?

mike_h: preparing canary. Patch candidate (configmap diff):
```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: ConfigMap
data:
  batch.max_size: "8"
  batch.flush_ms: "50"
  batch.priority: "latency"
```
Will patch streamer-pool-canary first.

lee_ops: FYI logs from packer show repeated "kv-cache-miss -> preemptive-evict" around the spike windows.
```
[2026-06-11T12:03:15Z] packer: enqueue seq_len=560
[2026-06-11T12:03:16Z] packer: flush batch_size=398 -> runtime: 5.3s
```
This matches mixed-seqlen amplification.

ops-bot: Incident severity updated to Sev2. Notifying product & SRE channels. Use INC-2026-1789 as incident ID.

mike_h: applying canary patch now to 2 nodes (streamer-canary-0, streamer-canary-1):
```
kubectl -n prod patch configmap runtime-streamer --patch '{"data":{"batch.max_size":"8","batch.flush_ms":"50"}}'
```

mike_h: canary applied. Monitoring.

oncall-bot: canary deployment completed on streamer-canary-0/1. Health checks green.

sara_p: metrics after canary (2m window): p99 on canary nodes ~620ms, non-canary still ~5.5s. Good signal.

lee_ops: can we expand to 50%? We'll stagger to avoid throughput cliffs.

nina_re: note: reducing batch size will increase token cost a bit. Documenting tradeoff in incident note.

tim_oncall: go ahead with 50% if metrics continue. I'll hold on paging customers — still no errors, only latency. Keep product informed.

mike_h: scaling rollout to 50% now. Command:
```
kubectl label nodes streamer-pool --overwrite rollout=latency-fix
helm upgrade streamer --set batch.max_size=8 --set batch.flush_ms=50 --namespace prod
```

ops-bot: patch rollout started. ETA ~6m.

mike_h: rollout 50% complete. Observed p99 cluster-wide drop: 5.7s -> 0.62s within ~4m of canary start. p95 steady.

sara_p: verified SLO dashboards: p99 for /v1/stream fell below SLO (was breaching) and now at 0.9s overall. Good.

lee_ops: logs show packer flush sizes reduced to <20, no huge burst flushes. Also saw fewer kv-evict events after change.

nina_re: created follow-up ticket: RWD-INC-2026-1789-FU for root cause (mixed-seqlen policy + batch sizing) and recommended long-term fixes: seqlen-aware packing, per-customer pacing.

tim_oncall: tagging infra for capacity review if we decide to revert later. For now, keep latency config. Escalation to eng-runtime lead if any regression.

mike_h: note — I've not rolled back the earlier kernel change; we only adjusted runtime config. We'll keep monitoring for 1h and then discuss permanent config or alternate approach (hedging small sequences, KV-cache prioritization).

ops-bot: Incident update: mitigation in place, SLOs recovering. Severity -> Sev3. Notifying stakeholders. :white_check_mark:

sara_p: summary for postmortem: deploy changed max_batch_size -> unintentionally amplified mixed-seqlen; immediate mitigation: cap batch size + lower flush interval. Action items: deploy seqlen-aware packer, add canary guard on batch-size increases, run load test with mixed seqlen.

mike_h: pushing notes to INC-2026-1789, will open PR for seqlen-aware packer.

tim_oncall: closing pager in 10m if stable. Thanks all for fast triage. :thumbsup:

oncall-bot: Pager closed by tim_oncall at 2026-06-11T12:13:09Z. Follow-up ticket: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/RWD-INC-2026-1789

sara_p: adding final reminder: postmortem due EOD tomorrow, include customer impact numbers and cost delta from smaller batches."
